BICYCLE: Biking is a great way to explore the city. From our apartment, all the south of Manhattan is accessible by bike, all the way to Brooklyn. There are plenty of City bike stations around. name: MODERN WILLIAMSBURG DUPLEX NEAR ALL THE ACTION
transit: L train is either 4 blocks or 7 blocks away, depending on whether you want to head to Manhattan or into Bushwick.  I always take the longer route because I like the walk, but if it's hot or it's raining, I use the closer stop.  The L will take you into Manhattan in 2 stops, and in 4 stops you're in Union Square.  Stay on for two more stops and you're in the Meat Packing District.   The J, M, Z is just as close and will take you to different parts of the city. name: Sweet and modern 2BR getaway in Bed-Stuy
transit: Nearest airports are LaGuardia (20 minutes) and JFK (30 minutes) most easily reached by taxi or Uber; Newark is a farther, more expensive ride. We are .4 miles from the J train (at Gates or Koszicusko) and .8 miles from the A/C train at Utica; on either train, it’s about 40 minutes to midtown Manhattan (59th St/Central Park) and less time to lower Manhattan. The A/C train also takes you most popular neighborhoods in Brooklyn (Prospect Heights, Clinton Hill, Ft Greene, downtown, Dumbo, Cobble Hill, Brooklyn Heights). There are also many buses. Parking is easy to find in Bed-Stuy— we drive all the time, all over Brooklyn— although cars do need to be parked on the correct side for street cleaning twice weekly. The Juno app is a great, local car service app (a better deal for drivers and quicker pick up than Uber), which we also use frequently for inter-Brooklyn travel.

name: Urban Zen in the Heart of Williamsburg
transit: The apartment is 10 ft from the L train-- you will be in Manhattan in under 5 minutes! *Please note: until March 18th, the L train is under construction and service will halt late nights and on weekends. There is still plenty of public transportation nearby. Also due to the construction, light sleepers may be disturbed in the morning by noise. I recommend bringing earplugs if you are sensitive to sound (I am, but with white noise I never hear them). The JMZ trains are about a 15-min walk. Buses are one block away, including the FREE L-train replacement bus which operates on certain nights and weekends when the L train is not running. The ferry is 10 minutes away and can take you to Manhattan and south Brooklyn. It's my personal favorite way to commute! It's also an easy drive in and out of the city or heading upstate. There is plenty of parking (both metered and lots) within a few blocks.

name: Charming BDR - 15min Manhattan-4min stn trains N,W
transit: If you have a car there is plenty of safe street parking in the neighborhood, but please pay close attention to the street cleaning signs as every other side of the street is cleaned every other day. The N and W subway trains run 24 hours and the closest stops are ¼ mile away (0.5 km) or a 5-minute walk. If you are staying in NYC longer than 5 days I suggest purchasing a 7-day unlimited ride pass so that you can use all subway trains and busses during your stay ($32). The subway stop is  located on 31st street & Ditmars BLVD. Exit the building and take a right , followed by another right on on Ditmars Blvd.  You will hit 31st street and then you will see Ditmars Blvd station. The N and w subway trains run above ground in Astoria. Midtown Manhattan is approximately 15-20 minutes away by subway.   If you want to use a taxi,  Taxi ride to midtown Manhattan costs about $20 and takes about 18/30 minutes depending on traffic.

transit: Obviously, this is the catch. How do you get to Manhattan!? You can either take a 10-15 minute walk (there are hills involved) to the Metro North train station. Public transit is much more complicated from the airports.   Or if you don’t mind being shuttled in an Toyota Corolla, I would be willing to drop you off in midtown west (57th street and 10th Avenue) if I’m heading to work. name: Enjoy Summer in the West Village.
transit: The apartment is easy to arrive at via car because Perry Street has its own exit off of the West Side Highway. In addition, there is street parking throughout the west village as well as plentiful garages for short-term and long-term parking. From the apartment, it's just a short walk (7-10 minutes) to the A,B,C,D,E,F,L,1,2, and 3 subway lines. These lines will provide easy access to uptown and downtown Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Queens. There is also a stop for the 8th Avenue bus on the corner outside, as well as the 14th Street bus a few blocks away. If you are so inclined, there is a bike share (CitiBike) station on the corner of the block also. The Hudson River Park is three blocks away and allows for beautiful walks and bike rides up and down the Hudson river. In less than 10 minutes, you can also walk to the Highline, a defunct subway line that has been turned into an elevated, green pedestrian park. Within 10 minutes are countless city parks, including Washington Square Park.

The G runs through Greenpoint and Williamsburg from Long Island City (Queens) and on to many other areas: Bed-Stuy, Clinton Hill, Downtown Brooklyn, Cobble Hill, Carroll Gardens, Gowanus and southern Park Slope. Bus The B32 and the B62 connect Greenpoint and Williamsburg; the latter services Clinton Hill, Fort Greene and downtown. The B43 and B48 go from Greenpoint through East Williamsburg and on to Bed-Stuy and Crown Heights. Ferry There are three stops in Greenpoint and Williamsburg on the East River NYC Ferry route, going to midtown and Lower Manhattan.
